personas.name: alice_happy_path
personas.goal: Alice logs in, reads her feed, creates a post, reads it back, edits it, reads it again, and deletes it.

personas.name: bob_follow_unfollow
personas.goal: Bob logs in, follows Dave, verifies follow, unfollows, verifies unfollow, and checks followers list.

personas.name: carol_profile_update
personas.goal: Carol logs in, updates her about_me and password with correct old_password, then verifies new password works.

personas.name: dave_pagination_power_user
personas.goal: Dave logs in and exercises pagination on posts, users, following, and followers with various limits and after cursors.

personas.name: erin_register_and_post
personas.goal: Erin registers a new account, logs in, creates a post, and reads the public posts list.

personas.name: frank_password_reset_flow
personas.goal: Frank requests a password reset, uses the returned token to set a new password, then logs in with it.

personas.name: careless_empty_post
personas.goal: Alice logs in and tries to create a post with empty text, expecting validation error.

personas.name: careless_long_post
personas.goal: Bob logs in and tries to create a post exceeding 280 characters, expecting validation error.

personas.name: careless_bad_pagination
personas.goal: Carol logs in and requests invalid pagination parameters (negative offset, zero limit, offset+after).

personas.name: careless_unknown_user_follow
personas.goal: Dave logs in and tries to follow/unfollow non-existent user ID 999, expecting 404.

personas.name: careless_duplicate_follow
personas.goal: Erin logs in and tries to follow Alice twice, expecting 409 on second attempt.

personas.name: careless_bad_password_change
personas.goal: Frank logs in and tries to change password without old_password and with wrong old_password, expecting 400.

personas.name: probe s1: user_alice
personas.goal: Test user profile and password exposure

personas.name: probe s2: user_bob
personas.goal: Test follower exposure and password hash in lists

personas.name: probe s3: user_carol
personas.goal: Test post author password hash exposure

personas.name: probe s4: user_dave
personas.goal: Test password_hash writeable input on update

personas.name: probe s5: user_erin
personas.goal: Test password_hash acceptance on user creation

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be exposed in API responses because ma.auto_field() defaults to dump_only=False, leaking password hashes to clients.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1 with valid Authorization header; check if response JSON contains a password_hash field with a non-null value.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 returned password_hash absent in base but present with a hash value in head.

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be exposed in the authenticated user's own profile response.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/me with valid Authorization header; check if response JSON contains a password_hash field.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me returned password_hash absent in base but present with hash values in head across multiple probes.

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be exposed in paginated user lists such as followers or following endpoints.
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1/followers with valid Authorization header; check if any user object in response.data contains a password_hash field.
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me/followers and GET /api/me/following returned password_hash absent in base but present (or null) in head for user objects in data array.

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be exposed in the user object nested inside post responses (author field).
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/posts/1 with valid Authorization header; check if response.json.author contains a password_hash field.
suspicions.evidence: Multiple post endpoints (feed, posts list, single post, create, update) returned author.password_hash absent in base but present (or null) in head.

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be accepted as writeable input on user creation or update, allowing clients to set password hashes directly.
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON body containing username, email, password, and password_hash fields; check if response contains the submitted password_hash or if a 400 validation error occurs.
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/users with password_hash in request body returned password_hash absent in base but present with submitted hash value in head.

suspicions.claim: The password_hash field may be accepted as writeable input on user profile update (PUT /api/me), allowing users to overwrite their password hash.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/me with Authorization header and JSON body containing password_hash; check if response contains the new password_hash or if the user's password changes to the hash value.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/me with password_hash in request body returned password_hash absent in base but present with new hash value in head.
